Repo: /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres hosting platform, prod DB, git repository). FIRST STEP: create your own isolated worktree by running, from /opt/nxeon: `git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wip-lifetime-spend -b fix/lifetime-spend-double-count` — then do ALL your work inside `/opt/nxeon-wip-lifetime-spend`, not the main /opt/nxeon tree. Do NOT merge into main and do NOT touch the live `/opt/nxeon` working tree directly — I will review your diff myself before it goes anywhere near production, since this touches financial reporting. (Node_modules: check whether the new worktree needs its own `npm install` or can reuse /opt/nxeon's via a symlink — follow whatever pattern this repo's other worktrees use; do not `git add -A` blindly in the worktree, a past incident here replaced prod's real node_modules with a self-referential symlink when that was done carelessly.)

## Confirmed bug (I already root-caused this by reading the code — do not re-derive it, just verify and act on it)

Nxeon's "lifetime spend" (shown on app/admin/users/[id]/page.tsx as `lifetimeSpendCents = paidInvoices.reduce((s,i) => s + (i.amountCents - i.refundedCents), 0)`, summing ALL PAID Invoice rows for a user) double-counts money.

Why: every real payment (Stripe/PayPal/Coinbase) first credits the customer's WALLET via `creditCheckoutSession` (lib/stripe.ts) or `creditExternalPayment` (lib/fulfil-checkout.ts) — this mints a `WalletTransaction` row with a POSITIVE `amountCents` and a non-null `stripeSessionId` (this column is reused for PayPal/Coinbase session ids too). If the payment is a genuine standalone top-up (not immediately funding a specific purchase — `isPurchaseLegSession` returns false), it ALSO creates a PAID Invoice ("Wallet top-up") documenting that real money arrived.

Separately, EVERY spend — an order (lib/order.ts), a renewal (worker/billing.ts's `commitRenewal`), a resize, a disk expand, a hosting/email/game order, a domain transfer, etc. — debits the wallet (`debitWallet` + a WalletTransaction with a NEGATIVE amountCents, no stripeSessionId) and ALSO creates its own PAID Invoice documenting the specific thing purchased, regardless of whether the money spent was fresh (same-moment purchase-leg) or OLD balance sitting in the wallet from an earlier top-up.

Concrete real example that triggered this investigation: customer tops up $15 (Invoice: "Wallet top-up", $15, PAID) then later buys an $8.88/mo VPS paying from wallet balance (Invoice: "Order: ... VPS ...", $8.88, PAID). Summing both invoices gives $23.88 "lifetime spend" when the customer only ever gave Nxeon $15. The WalletTransaction ledger is correct throughout (+1500, then -888, leaving a $6.12 balance, matching the real balance shown in the admin UI) — the bug is purely in how "lifetime spend"/revenue is DERIVED from Invoice rows instead of from the wallet ledger.

Confirmed NOT double-counted by non-revenue wallet credits: `lib/actions-growth.ts` referral bonuses and `lib/actions-admin-billing.ts`'s manual admin balance adjustment (`billing.adjust_balance`, the admin "Credit" button) both create WalletTransaction rows with amountCents > 0 but NO `stripeSessionId` — so filtering on `stripeSessionId IS NOT NULL` correctly excludes free/promotional credits from "real revenue".

Refunds: `lib/actions-admin-billing.ts`'s `refundPayment` increments `Invoice.refundedCents` on the specific invoice being refunded (when an invoiceId is targeted, which is the normal/current UI path) — this is the authoritative "how much of what was billed has been given back" figure, independent of whether the refund route was a real Stripe refund or a wallet-balance correction. The refund flow does NOT create a new stripeSessionId-tagged WalletTransaction, so it will not naturally show up as negative in a stripeSessionId-filtered sum — it must be subtracted separately via `Invoice.refundedCents`.

## The correct formula (verified by hand-tracing the code, implement this exactly)

**Real net lifetime revenue for a user = SUM(WalletTransaction.amountCents WHERE amountCents > 0 AND stripeSessionId IS NOT NULL) − SUM(Invoice.refundedCents across that user's invoices)**

This correctly gives $15.00 for the example customer above (email `jsj8013@gmail.com` in production — you can query the real DB to confirm: their WalletTransaction rows should show +1500 with a stripeSessionId set, and -888 with none; their two invoices should NOT both count).

## What to build

1. A shared, well-documented helper — put it in `lib/revenue.ts` (new file) or alongside other financial helpers if you find a more idiomatic home (check `lib/wallet.ts`, `lib/invoices.ts` first for precedent). Needs:
   - A single-user version: `realLifetimeSpendCents(userId: string): Promise<number>` for the admin user detail page.
   - A BATCHED version for admin list pages that need this for many users at once (e.g. `realLifetimeSpendCentsByUser(userIds: string[]): Promise<Map<string,number>>`), using Prisma `groupBy`/aggregate — NOT N+1 queries. Check how existing admin list pages batch similar per-user aggregates (grep for `groupBy` usage in app/admin/) for the established pattern.
   - Document the WHY (the double-counting mechanism above) directly in the code comment, the way this codebase's existing financial code does (see lib/wallet-split.ts, lib/renewal-charge.ts, lib/order.ts for the house style of "explain the incident/reasoning, not just the mechanism").

2. Fix `app/admin/users/[id]/page.tsx`'s `lifetimeSpendCents` computation (currently at or near line 95) to use the new single-user helper instead of the naive invoice sum. Verify the rendered page still shows invoice COUNT correctly (that part — `user._count.invoices` — is fine as-is, it's a real count of billing documents, not a money sum; do not change it).

3. AUDIT (read carefully, do not blindly find-and-replace) every one of these files for the SAME bug pattern (summing Invoice.amountCents / aggregating invoices as if that equals "revenue" or "lifetime spend" or "total received"):
   - app/admin/billing/page.tsx
   - app/admin/subscriptions/page.tsx
   - app/admin/analytics/page.tsx
   - app/admin/accounting/page.tsx
   - app/admin/invoices/page.tsx
   - app/admin/domains/page.tsx
   - app/admin/gift-codes/page.tsx
   - app/admin/partners/page.tsx
   - app/admin/partners/[id]/page.tsx
   - app/admin/affiliate/page.tsx
   - lib/spend-caps.ts
   - lib/actions-affiliate.ts
   - lib/affiliate.ts
   - lib/actions-partner.ts
   - lib/partner-commission.ts

   For EACH file, determine intent before touching anything:
   - If the sum is genuinely meant to represent "real money the business received" / "revenue" / "a customer's lifetime spend" — THIS is the bug, fix it to use the new helper (or the same underlying formula inline/batched, whichever fits the page's existing query shape better).
   - If the sum is legitimately about something else that should NOT change — e.g. "total value of goods invoiced" for a display/audit purpose, a commission base that's contractually defined against invoiced amounts rather than net cash received, a spend-cap/fraud-throttle that intentionally wants to catch high invoice VOLUME regardless of funding source, gift-code redemption totals, affiliate/partner commission calculations that were designed around invoice totals on purpose — leave it alone. Do not "fix" something that isn't actually the revenue bug just because it touches Invoice.amountCents.
   - When genuinely unsure whether a given sum represents real revenue vs. something else, err toward LEAVING IT ALONE and flag it clearly in your final report for me to decide, rather than guessing on financial/commission logic that could affect what partners/affiliates are owed.

4. Do NOT touch any actual money-movement code — lib/order.ts, lib/stripe.ts, lib/fulfil-checkout.ts, worker/billing.ts, lib/wallet.ts, lib/actions-admin-billing.ts's refund logic, etc. This is a REPORTING/ANALYTICS-ONLY fix. The underlying WalletTransaction/Invoice architecture is correct and intentional (I read the extensive comments justifying it) — only how downstream pages DERIVE totals from it is wrong.

## Verification (required before you report back)

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
2. `npm test` — compare against this EXACT current baseline of 34 pre-existing failing tests (all unrelated pricing/proration/auth-baseline tests, not touched by this work): "the server charge path still composes promoPriceCents(vpsTermPriceCents(...))", "payAndDeploy RESERVES the credit before opening the Checkout session", "every route that rate-limits sources its IP from the trusted helper", "opening the session is passed the hold token, and a failed open RELEASES the hold", "the sold-rate basis and catalogue this file is pinned to have not moved", "upgrading on day one costs exactly the difference between the two fresh orders", "a stacked expiry round-trips to zero — the $362.88 cap asymmetry", "promo-window arbitrage: upgrading at 45% and downgrading at 10% is not a business", "lib/proration.ts may never read the clock or the promo calendar for a price", "renewing early blends the rate instead of repricing the discounted months", "every path that sells, renews or gifts a term records the rate it was sold at", "the money a game downgrade WOULD credit exceeds what was collected", "the renewal quote charges the term it advertises, not a month", "re-pricing a paid order at a different basis moves real money", "a sold price round-trips through Stripe metadata unchanged", "the settled total does not move when the promo rotates under it", "a malformed stamped price is refused outright rather than half-believed", "the order path stamps the price before the card is charged and settles it after", "the promo bar reads its headline price from the catalogue, never a literal", "a game server renews at its FLAT game-plan price, not the base VPS plan's", "B4: signing up and browsing are NOT gated — only buying is", "HAZARD: every export of a \"use server\" module is authenticated, or explicitly anonymous", "no NEW call site keys anything on the caller-supplied first hop", "privileged admin writes reach for staff authority, not bare requireUser", "vpsTerm returns the matching term by months", "vpsTermPriceCents applies commitment discounts", "vpsTermPriceCents rounds to whole cents", "vpsEffectiveMonthly reflects the discounted per-month price", "every fulfilment failure that captured money notifies the customer", "payAndDeploy hands its own quote to checkout instead of letting it re-quote", "fpm pool: hardened limits, open_basedir scoped to home, no /tmp", "the empty games page offers a support link, not a dead 'contact support'", "a partial discount composes in ONE order only — on the term total, not the monthly", "the recurring figure on a term card is the renewal price, never the promo price". Your change must not add ANY new failures beyond this list, and ideally add new passing tests for the new helper (a wallet-top-up-then-spend scenario, a referral-credit scenario that must NOT count, a refund scenario that must reduce the total).
3. Directly query the production-shaped DB (check `.env`/`DATABASE_URL` in your worktree before running any query, and use READ-ONLY `SELECT`/Prisma `findMany` for verification, never write) for the user with email `jsj8013@gmail.com` and confirm your new helper returns $15.00 (1500 cents) for their lifetime spend, not $23.88.

## Final report format

For each of the 15 audited files: one line — filename, verdict (FIXED / LEFT ALONE / FLAGGED FOR YOUR DECISION), one-sentence reasoning. Then the verification results (tsc, test diff, the $15.00 confirmation query result). Then list every file you created or modified, and confirm the worktree path/branch name.
